title: Adoption Signal Bucketizer and Calibration Notes
summary: Working notes and calibration procedure for converting raw adoption signals into discrete buckets, applying weights, and tuning final health score probabilities. Focused on non-linear signal transforms, signal interaction heuristics, and a small-sample calibration loop for high-value accounts.
body:
Purpose:
- Create a repeatable step-by-step for turning raw telemetry and engagement metrics into a calibrated health probability used in CS workflows and renewal risk triage.
- Primary audience: CS data analysts, CSMs running risk reviews, and product managers wanting to understand how scores move.

Background and constraints:
- We already ingest 40+ telemetry features (API calls, model throughput, average prompt tokens, failed requests, feature flags used, console logins). Most are noisy; we need robust buckets that generalize across seat sizes and LTV.
- Goal health output: 0-1 probability of near-term (90-day) renewal risk. We want monotonicity (more usage -> lower risk), explainability (top 3 contributing signals), and sensitivity tuning for Enterprise vs. SMB cohorts.

Signal catalog (selected for this iteration):
1) Daily active endpoints (dae): unique API keys observed in last 7d.
2) Median tokens per request (med_tok): rolling 14d median.
3) Error rate (err_pct): % requests with 5xx / client errors, 7d window.
4) Console logins per user-week (console_freq).
5) Feature adoption index (feat_idx): count of opt-ins for major features (reranking, caching, streaming) normalized by org size.
6) Model switch frequency (model_freq): number of distinct model versions used in 30d - high value when frequent changes (indicates active experimentation).

Bucketization approach (why buckets):
- Buckets reduce sensitivity to spikes and make the score explainable to CSM.
- Use quantile bucketing for highly skewed signals (dae, med_tok), and fixed thresholds for operational signals (err_pct).

Proposed buckets (initial):
- dae buckets: [0, 1-2, 3-9, 10-49, 50+] labeled B0..B4 (string labels used in UI).
- med_tok buckets: [0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025-4096, 4097+] B0..B4.
- err_pct thresholds: [>=5% => high risk, 1-5% => medium risk, <1% => low risk] => map to risk-adjusters +0.25, +0.1, 0.0.
- console_freq: [0, 1, 2-4, 5+] (low to high engagement).
- feat_idx: integer 0..N, treat as linear until N=5 then saturate.

Raw bucket to score mapping (base weights):
- Base bucket weights (pre-normalization):
  dae B0..B4 => [0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.15, 0.02]  # lower is lower risk value contribution
  med_tok B0..B4 => [0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1]
  console_freq B0..B3 => [0.75, 0.45, 0.25, 0.05]
  feat_idx linear contribution => weight = max(0, 0.6 - 0.08*(5 - feat_idx)) capped at 0.05 min

- err_pct acts as a multiplier on aggregated score: if err_pct >=5% multiply final_prob by 1.6 (increase risk), if 1-5% multiply by 1.15, else 1.0.

Combining function (prototype):
1) Map each signal to its bucket score s_i in [0,1] (0 -> low risk, 1 -> high risk). Our bucket weights above are risk-values (smaller means lower risk). We'll invert to risk-probability p_i = normalize(1 - s_i) so higher p_i => healthier.
2) Weighted geometric mean across signals to preserve multiplicative interactions:
   health_raw = exp(sum(w_i * ln(p_i + eps))) where eps=1e-6 to avoid zero.
   weights w_i sum to 1.
3) Apply error-rate multiplier m_err to produce health_adj = health_raw / m_err (dividing because multiplier >1 means higher risk => lower health).
4) Convert to renewal_risk = 1 - health_adj (clamp 0..1).

Why geometric mean?
- It penalizes single critical failures (e.g., zero feature adoption or very high errors) more than arithmetic mean. This fits business need: one bad signal should be able to trigger high risk.

Calibration procedure (small-sample loop for v0):
1) Select calibration cohort: 300 recent accounts that had renewal decision in last 180 days (mix SMB, Mid, Enterprise).
2) Compute health_adj for each account using frozen bucket thresholds and weights.
3) Bin accounts by health_adj deciles and compute observed renewal rate per bin.
4) Fit isotonic regression or Platt scaling (logistic) to map health_adj -> P(renew). Choose isotonic if non-parametric shape preferred. Store calibration mapping as lookup table.
5) Evaluate Brier score, ROC-AUC for predicting churn (non-renew within 90 days).
6) Iterate: adjust bucket thresholds where calibration residuals high, re-weight signals that consistently under/over predict.

Worked example (toy):
- Account A: dae=12 (B3 -> base weight 0.15), med_tok=320 (B2 -> 0.3), console_freq=0 (B0 -> 0.75), feat_idx=2 (weight ~0.44), err_pct=0.8% (multiplier 1.0).
  Map to p_i (1 - s_i normalized): use simplest normalize by dividing by max weight (0.8) then invert.
  Rough p_values: dae p=1 - 0.15/0.8 = 0.8125; med_tok p=1 - 0.3/0.8 = 0.625; console p=1 - 0.75/0.8 = 0.0625; feat p ~ 1 - 0.44/0.8 = 0.45.
  geometric mean (weights equal for now) => health_raw ~ 0.27 => health_adj ~0.27 => renewal_risk ~0.73 (high risk because console_freq=0 dominates).

Policy mapping and playbook hooks (CS workflow):
- Health bands: Healthy (health_adj >= 0.75), Watch (0.4 <= health_adj < 0.75), Risk (health_adj < 0.4).
- For accounts in Watch: automated playbooks email CSM with top 3 negative contributors and suggested actions (monitor caching, suggest quantization changes, run onboarding workshop).
- For Risk and ARR > $100k: immediate 1:1 outreach + technical deep-dive + renewal-as-a-service offer.
- Add 'escalation"): if err_pct >=10% or system-wide incident tag present, mark urgent regardless of health band.

Explainability: top-3 contributors computed by delta-if-removed heuristic:
- For each signal i: compute health_adj_i_removed by setting signal to cohort median then recompute health; contributor_score_i = health_adj_i_removed - health_adj. Largest positive deltas are highest negative contributors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we treat model_freq as positive (experimentation) or negative (instability)? Need cohort analysis.
- Feature adoption index currently favors org size-normalized counts; explore per-seat adoption or weighted by feature importance.
- Look into time-decay for signals: older activity should count less for renewal prediction. Candidate half-life: 21 days.
- Evaluate alternative aggregators: min-based aggregator for safety-critical customers.

Next steps (next 4 weeks):
- Run calibration cohort extract (data request CS-ENG-REQ-048). Owner: Lucas. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Implement geometric-mean aggregator in model eval notebook. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Create initial isotonic map and compute Brier and AUC. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-03-24.
- Draft CSM playbook snippets and email templates for Watch and Risk bands. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-03-31.

Appendix: quick CSV-like table for signal debug (columns):
org_id, dae, med_tok, err_pct, console_freq, feat_idx, model_freq, raw_health_adj, calibrated_p_renew, renewal_decision
ACME-123, 12, 320, 0.8, 0, 2, 1, 0.27, 0.22, NO
BLOOM-88, 54, 1400, 0.2, 7, 4, 3, 0.82, 0.79, YES
SMB-77, 1, 40, 2.5, 0, 0, 0, 0.11, 0.08, NO

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Avoid very aggressive weights on single usage signals for enterprise customers; they tend to have irregular spikes. Instead rely more on console activity and feature adoption.
- For small accounts (<$10k ARR) favor simpler linear model to reduce overfitting.
